memberOmissions.name: Finalize
memberOmissions.reason: Swift deinit is non-public lifetime syntax and not a callable member

parameterLabels.constructors: class constructor labels preserve CLR metadata names; value-type constructor external labels are _
parameterLabels.methods: first external label is _; later labels preserve CLR metadata names

primaryAssociatedTypeMapping: CLR interface generic parameters map to same-named Swift primary associated types
protocolWitnessMapping: A public Swift conformance witness forced by a CLR explicit interface implementation is compiler-measured through sourceOrigin and excluded from the concrete type member count
arrayMutationMapping: CLR caller-owned destination arrays named destinationArray or corners, plus ICollection<T>.CopyTo array destinations, map to Swift inout Array; source arrays remain value snapshots
collectionCopyToArrayMutationMapping: A CopyTo array parameter on a type whose direct CLR interface is ICollection<T> or IList<T> is caller-owned mutable destination storage. IList<T> inherits ICollection<T>, so the destination and the inout projection are the same
enumerableMapping: System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<T> parameters map to Swift Array<T>
enumeratorReturnMapping: System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerator<T> returns map to CNAEnumerator<T>, whose throwing Next preserves live order and mutation invalidation without a fake Microsoft collection type
eventMapping: A CLR event whose type is System.EventHandler<TArgs> maps to exactly one get-only Swift property preserving the XNA event name, of type CNAEvent<TArgs>. The add_/remove_/raise_ accessors are CLR encoding, not XNA identities, and must not appear in the Swift surface. CNAEvent exposes only Add and Remove; the raise capability lives on the separate CNAEventSource, which is composed with CNAEvent over private storage and must never subclass it, so a consumer holding a CNAEvent cannot downcast its way to Raise. Add returns an opaque CNAEventSubscription token: CLR Delegate.Remove matches on delegate identity, which Swift closures do not have, so token-based removal is the LANGUAGE_PROJECTION of that rule and differs from CLR in that duplicate registrations of one closure are independently removable.
existentialSpelling: Swift emits a CLR interface-typed member as the existential `any P`, which is the same type as `P`, so the spelling normalizes away. The opaque `some P` is a different type and is not normalized.
measuredSupportBaseMapping: A non-XNA CLR base listed in measuredSupportBaseProjections is a MEASURED base, exactly as an XNA base is: the Swift type must be a class whose compiler-emitted superclass is the mapped support type. A missing base, AnyObject or Object in its place, a struct where the CLR declares a class, a different support base, or any other base projection is a BASE_MAPPING_MISMATCH. It is never silently dropped and never allowlisted.
eventSupportMapping: The event support types live outside Microsoft.Xna.Framework and are language-support API, not XNA types or XNA identities, so they are counted in no XNA scoreboard. They are nevertheless MEASURED against the pinned shape above: an absent support type is an UNMEASURED_STRUCTURAL_CATEGORY, and a wrong kind, wrong generic arity, a base where composition is required, a missing required member, or a forbidden member is an EVENT_MAPPING_MISMATCH. Pointer, opaque-handle and CNA FFI spellings inside a support type remain RAW_HANDLE_LEAK and PUBLIC_NATIVE_FFI_LEAK.
nullableMapping: System.Nullable<T> maps to Swift T?; ref/out direction remains independently mapped to inout
intPtrLanguageProjection: System.IntPtr maps to Swift Int: the opaque pointer-width signed numeric value of the CLR IntPtr, and IntPtr.Zero maps to 0. It is a LANGUAGE PROJECTION and is not a Swift pointer, a dereferenceable address, a CNA native handle, an SDL window, or proof that the value is valid. The expected projection is never RAW_HANDLE_LEAK; UnsafeRawPointer, UnsafeMutableRawPointer, OpaquePointer and native-handle wrappers remain leaks, and a fixed-width Int64 or an unsigned UInt substitute remains a mapping mismatch. RAW_HANDLE_LEAK stays required at zero.
indexedPropertyAccessorMapping: A read/write CLR indexed property maps to a throwing Item getter plus throwing SetItem method; the verifier combines both compiler symbols into one source property identity
throwsMapping: Swift throws is LANGUAGE_MAPPING and does not add an XNA member
nonPublicConstructionMapping: A public CLR class whose declared constructors are all non-public is not externally derivable, so it maps to a Swift public class that is neither open nor final unless the CLR type is sealed; any Swift initializer it needs stays internal implementation infrastructure and must not appear as a public init in the Symbol Graph
inheritedPublicMemberProjection: A selected public inherited member may be declared on a partial Swift subtype until its XNA base exists; the verifier requires an exact ancestor identity. System.IDisposable maps to a public Dispose() member.
nestedTypeMapping: replace CLR + nesting separator with Swift . nesting

systemInterfaceMappings.System.IEquatable`1: Equals/operator members; no Swift Equatable conformance required
systemInterfaceMappings.System.IComparable`1: CompareTo(T) member; no Swift Comparable conformance or language-added ordering operators
systemInterfaceMappings.System.IDisposable: Dispose member; no public helper protocol
systemInterfaceMappings.System.Collections.Generic.ICollection`1: the concrete XNA Add/Clear/Contains/CopyTo/Remove/Count/IsReadOnly members represent the direct interface; no automatic Swift Collection conformance
systemInterfaceMappings.System.Collections.Generic.IList`1: the concrete XNA members represent the direct interface: the seven inherited ICollection<T> members plus IndexOf/Insert/RemoveAt and the indexed Item; no automatic Swift Collection, MutableCollection or RandomAccessCollection conformance
systemInterfaceMappings.System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable`1: GetEnumerator maps to CNAEnumerator<T>; no automatic Swift Sequence conformance
systemInterfaceMappings.System.Collections.IEnumerable: GetEnumerator mapping only; no automatic Swift Sequence conformance
